finding: Test 14 says "The two surviving assertions of the gate guard still pass". The round-7 snapshot said nine, and nine is the measured number: internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go:469-503 carries eleven assert/require calls (:473, :474, :481, :484, :485, :490, :493, :494, :497, :498, :500) and the reversal is :473-:474 only, so 9 survive. The rewrite also contradicts its own §6, which says "Every other assertion in those guards stands". As written, test 14 is satisfied by an implementation that keeps two assertions and deletes seven, including :498's assert.Len(t, e, 3, ...) — which spec/0.34.0.tasks.json records as the mutation-killing assertion in this file.
suggestion: Restore the measured number: "The nine surviving assertions of TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate still pass", or bind the claim to the artifact instead of a literal ("every assert/require in the guard other than the two reversed at :473-:474") so it cannot rot the way this one just did.

finding: The snapshot named three of the guard's surviving assertions explicitly and said why: "three of them are named here because a unit with spec cover for 'reversing the guard' could otherwise delete them" — that a wontfix disposition does not clear an open finding (:485-:487), that --check stays shut over a disposed finding (:490), and :498's assert.Len(t, e, 3). It also recorded the one real dependency (only :490 needs §2's fail-closed rule, because signalRow emits no severity key) and the forward note that spec/0.46.0.md §8.4's reset will touch :498. The rewrite replaces all of this with "Every other assertion in those guards stands". That sentence is a survey-free restatement, but the naming was not survey — it was the protection, earned in an earlier round, against exactly the deletion this release's own reversal licenses.
suggestion: Keep one sentence naming the three protected assertions and the :490 dependency in §6. They are boundary statements about what the release may not change, not citations that a later round can re-falsify.

finding: The rewrite renumbered the sections and reordered the Non-Goals, and three live pointers in spec/0.46.0.md now resolve to the wrong text. (1) 0.46.0.md:334 — "The breakdown on tp audit --merge is not deferred: spec/0.37.0.md Non-Goal 6 takes it". Non-Goal 6 is now "A fourth row status"; the breakdown moved to §4 and Non-Goal 4. (2) 0.46.0.md:332 — "An earlier draft of this paragraph said tp emits no count at all; that was false and spec/0.37.0.md §2 said so on the same day". The correction now lives in §4; the current §2 does not say it. (3) 0.46.0.md:384 — "the sentence is here because it was written in spec/0.37.0.md §3 and lost in the cut". §3 is now "The fence"; the cut is §5. All three break silently, because each still resolves to a real section.

Since spec/0.46.0.md is unshipped, editing it is permitted; leaving it is not, because a pointer that resolves to the wrong section is worse than a dangling one.

finding: §3 newly extends the fence to tp import — "Every path that writes the field under TP_UNATTENDED=1 exits 2 — including tp import" — and test 11 pins it for both all and blocking. tp import does not reach fenceWorkflowWrite at all; it assigns the whole workflow block (importcmd.go:158-162 via importedHasWorkflowKey), and when the imported document carries NO workflow key it copies the EXISTING file's block forward: tf.Workflow = existing.Workflow. So once a project has ever set audit_converge_on, every later import re-writes it, and a fence on "writes the field" refuses every subsequent import. Under tp run that is CLAUDE.md Workflow A step 6, so the release's own opt-in users would deadlock their decompose→import step on a value that changes nothing. The spec never distinguishes setting the field from carrying it forward, and nothing in the round-7 snapshot required tp import to be fenced at all — its fence sentence closed over tp set --workflow and its --project form.
suggestion: State the boundary the fence is over: a write that CHANGES the resolved value, or an explicit occurrence of the key in the imported document (importedHasWorkflowKey already computes exactly that), not a preserved carry-forward. Test 11 should pin the preserving import as exit 0, otherwise the release ships a deadlock for the projects that opt in.

finding: The snapshot carried a measured negative result about the fence mechanism and the rewrite dropped it with the survey: fenceWorkflowWrite has signature (field string, requested float64) — numeric by signature — and all four call sites (set.go:414, set.go:428, set_project.go:98, set_project.go:108) sit after ParseFloat/Atoi, so a string field reaches none of them. Still true in the tree today. The snapshot's conclusion was that "widening the numeric fence" ships a SILENT no-op and that the string-shaped fence to copy is the FencedCommandField guard placed before the type dispatch. §3 now says only "Every path that writes the field under TP_UNATTENDED=1 exits 2", which is the decision — but the natural implementation of that decision is the one measured not to work, and test 11 (exit 2 per path) would redden rather than pass, costing a cycle to rediscover. This is not a citation a later round re-falsifies; it is a negative result, and negative results are what CLAUDE.md's "prove a fix by running it" rule exists to preserve.
suggestion: Keep one sentence: the fence is not a widening of the numeric cap fence, which a string value never reaches. It is a decision about mechanism selection, not a survey of line numbers, and it survives without any citation.

finding: §3's escalation paragraph kept the decision (add audit-converge-on to the --decision enum) but dropped the boundary that came with it. The enum is closed over five values (engine/escalation.go:21-27, with the comment at :19 reading "not a sixth category") and its cardinality is asserted in several places that must move together; more importantly, the snapshot recorded that spec/0.35.0.md:428-429 closes the set over five, is a SHIPPED spec, and is therefore "recorded as superseded rather than edited" — citing spec/0.34.0.md Non-Goal 6, which forbids editing a shipped spec. That is a rule about what this release may not touch, i.e. exactly the kind of statement §6 exists for, and it is now nowhere in the file. A unit told to "add audit-converge-on to that enum" and finding a shipped spec that closes the set over five has no instruction not to edit it.
suggestion: Add a clause to §3 or a seventh Non-Goal: the enum grows to six and every shipped spec that closes it over five is recorded as superseded, not edited. The count of assertion sites can go to task acceptance; the don't-edit-a-shipped-spec boundary cannot.

finding: The header states the cut as a relocation — "the forensics that would guide an implementer go to spec/0.37.0.tasks.json" — in the present tense, as something done. spec/0.37.0.tasks.json does not exist (spec/ holds 25 .tasks.json files and none for 0.37.0), and cannot yet: decomposition follows convergence. So the survey was deleted, not moved, and between now and decomposition nothing in the repository carries it — the three instances above (the numeric-fence no-op, the shipped-spec boundary, the named surviving assertions) are already lost rather than parked. The sentence also makes the relocation unfalsifiable at review time, which is how three measured items left the tree in one commit without a round noticing.
suggestion: Phrase it as an obligation on the decomposition rather than as an accomplished move — "the forensics belong in spec/0.37.0.tasks.json's acceptance and are recorded in spec/.tp-review/0.37.0/snapshot-round-7.md until it exists" — so the snapshot is named as the interim home and the claim is checkable.

finding: 35a9d0f repairs round 7's finding of this class only for this working tree, and the published half is unchanged. Re-measured by running the hook against shimmed binaries: a tp reporting v0.36.0 — what `go install github.com/deligoez/tp/cmd/tp@latest` resolves to, since v0.36.0 is the newest tag — exits 2 with "tp v0.36.0 ... is older than the tp plugin's minimum 0.36.1" plus an install hint that cannot satisfy it; a tp reporting the tree's Go pseudo-version v0.36.1-0.2026...-35a9d0f exits 0. So 0.36.1 works precisely because Go's pseudo-version for a commit after v0.36.0 bumps the patch — it is a build artifact, not a version that will ever be tagged (the plan goes v0.36.0 → v0.37.0). marketplace.json's source is "./", so anyone running `claude plugin update tp@tp` before the v0.37.0 tag still gets a manifest demanding a binary that does not exist. The blast radius shrank from a minor version to a patch; the defect did not close.
suggestion: Either move the bump to immediately before the tag (round 7's suggestion, unaddressed), or state in CLAUDE.md's 4b that a mid-cycle bump is deliberately pinned to the Go pseudo-version of the development window and that external plugin users are refused until the tag — so the choice is recorded rather than rediscovered next cycle.

finding: 35a9d0f left internal/cli/plugin_test.go:25-47 as one contiguous comment block with no separator, so the whole eighteen-line paragraph documenting pluginMinVersion — including "It is READ from the manifest rather than restated beside it" and the account of the gate run that cost — is now the doc comment of `const preflightFloor = "0.35.0"`, a value that IS restated beside the thing it guards. The func pluginMinVersion at :49 has no doc comment at all. godoc and any reader taking the comment at face value get the two constants' rationales swapped, and the one sentence that most needs to stay attached to pluginMinVersion is the one now attached to its opposite.
suggestion: Insert a blank line before line 43 so the pluginMinVersion paragraph sits above func pluginMinVersion (or move it there), leaving preflightFloor's own three sentences as its comment.

finding: Two near-misses caught before they were written. (1) `faster_search` for the literal "0.36.1" across the repository root returned 0 matches on two runs, including with fresh=true, while .claude-plugin/plugin.json:3 plainly holds it — the walk excludes dot-directories by default, so .claude-plugin/, .tp/ and .github/ are invisible to any default search. I was one step from reporting the new version as inconsistent or unreferenced on that zero-match; no_ignore=true returns seven hits. Any corpus-wide count run over this repository without no_ignore silently omits the plugin manifest, the role corpus and CI. (2) I nearly filed §7 test 14's "two surviving assertions" as a plain arithmetic slip. Counting the guard first (eleven assert/require calls at audit_signal_test.go:473,474,481,484,485,490,493,494,497,498,500) is what showed it also contradicts §6's "every other assertion in those guards stands", which is the half that makes it high rather than low.
suggestion: When a spec or a review asserts a count over this repository, run the count with no_ignore and say which directories were in scope. And count the artifact before reporting a number as wrong — the count is what distinguishes a typo from a scope regression.
